part.text: The data can show annual motorist deaths and crash-based proxies, but it has no vehicle-miles-traveled measure, so it cannot directly establish risk per mile. The 2013 and 2025 records each cover a full calendar year; I’m comparing both the death counts and two distinct crash-based measures.

+from pathlib import Path
+import json
+
+import duckdb
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import pandas as pd
+
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+OUT = ROOT / "out"
+OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+
+query = """
+SELECT
+    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM crash_date)::INTEGER AS year,
+    COUNT(*)::INTEGER AS reported_crashes,
+    SUM(COALESCE(number_of_motorist_killed, 0))::INTEGER AS motorist_deaths,
+    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE COALESCE(number_of_motorist_killed, 0) > 0)::INTEGER
+        AS crashes_with_motorist_death
+FROM read_parquet(?)
+WHERE crash_date >= DATE '2013-01-01' AND crash_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
+GROUP BY 1
+ORDER BY 1
+"""
+data = duckdb.connect().execute(query, [str(ROOT / "data" / "crashes.parquet")]).fetchdf()
+data["motorist_deaths_per_1000_crashes"] = (
+    data["motorist_deaths"] / data["reported_crashes"] * 1000
+)
+data["pct_crashes_with_motorist_death"] = (
+    data["crashes_with_motorist_death"] / data["reported_crashes"] * 100
+)
+
+styles = [
+    {
+        "id": 1,
+        "metric": "Annual count of motorist deaths in reported crashes",
+        "denominator": "None (annual count)",
+        "grouping": "Calendar year",
+        "chart_type": "Line chart",
+        "column": "motorist_deaths",
+        "y_label": "Motorist deaths",
+        "title": "Motorist deaths in NYC reported crashes by year",
+        "reason": "A count directly shows how many motorist deaths were recorded each year, without implying an exposure denominator.",
+        "probability": 0.2,
+        "answer_template": "This data cannot determine deaths per mile; recorded motorist deaths fell from {a} in 2013 to {b} in 2025.",
+        "interpretation": "This framing answers how the annual number of motorist deaths in reported NYC crashes changed, and the chart shows the count fell between 2013 and 2025. A count is defensible as a direct burden measure, but it leaves both driving exposure and per-mile risk unanswered.",
+    },
+    {
+        "id": 2,
+        "metric": "Motorist deaths per 1,000 reported crashes",
+        "denominator": "All police-reported crashes in the same calendar year",
+        "grouping": "Calendar year",
+        "chart_type": "Line chart",
+        "column": "motorist_deaths_per_1000_crashes",
+        "y_label": "Motorist deaths per 1,000 reported crashes",
+        "title": "Motorist deaths per 1,000 NYC reported crashes",
+        "reason": "Normalizing deaths by reported crashes provides a crash-based severity proxy that accounts for changes in crash volume.",
+        "probability": 0.45,
+        "answer_template": "This data cannot determine deaths per mile; deaths per 1,000 reported crashes rose from {a:.2f} in 2013 to {b:.2f} in 2025.",
+        "interpretation": "This framing answers whether motorist deaths changed relative to the volume of reported crashes, and the chart shows this crash-based rate increased between 2013 and 2025. It is defensible for comparing fatality burden per reported crash, but does not measure travel exposure or deaths per mile driven.",
+    },
+    {
+        "id": 3,
+        "metric": "Share of reported crashes with at least one motorist death",
+        "denominator": "All police-reported crashes in the same calendar year",
+        "grouping": "Calendar year",
+        "chart_type": "Line chart",
+        "column": "pct_crashes_with_motorist_death",
+        "y_label": "Crashes with a motorist death (%)",
+        "title": "Share of NYC reported crashes with a motorist death",
+        "reason": "The fatal-crash share measures how often a reported crash involved a motorist death, without counting multiple deaths in one crash multiple times.",
+        "probability": 0.35,
+        "answer_template": "This data cannot determine deaths per mile; the share of reported crashes with a motorist death rose from {a:.3f}% in 2013 to {b:.3f}% in 2025.",
+        "interpretation": "This framing answers how frequently a police-reported crash involved any motorist death, and the chart shows that share increased between 2013 and 2025. It is defensible as a crash-level fatality measure, but it leaves vehicle-miles traveled and the per-mile risk unanswered.",
+    },
+]
+
+options = []
+for style in styles:
+    ident = style["id"]
+    column = style["column"]
+    values = data[["year", column]].copy()
+    values.columns = ["year", style["metric"].replace(" ", "_").lower()]
+    # Keep the metric and its denominator visible in the plotted data for auditability.
+    if ident == 1:
+        values["reported_crashes"] = data["reported_crashes"]
+    elif ident == 2:
+        values["motorist_deaths"] = data["motorist_deaths"]
+        values["reported_crashes"] = data["reported_crashes"]
+    else:
+        values["crashes_with_motorist_death"] = data["crashes_with_motorist_death"]
+        values["reported_crashes"] = data["reported_crashes"]
+    csv_path = OUT / f"values_{ident}.csv"
+    values.to_csv(csv_path, index=False, float_format="%.6f")
+
+    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5.3))
+    ax.plot(data["year"], data[column], marker="o", linewidth=2, color="#1769aa")
+    ax.set_xticks(data["year"])
+    ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=45)
+    ax.set_ylabel(style["y_label"])
+    ax.set_xlabel("Crash year")
+    ax.set_title(style["title"])
+    ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.3)
+    ax.text(
+        0.01,
+        -0.24,
+        "Source: NYC police-reported crash records. This dataset does not include miles driven.",
+        transform=ax.transAxes,
+        fontsize=8,
+        color="#555555",
+    )
+    fig.tight_layout()
+    fig.savefig(OUT / f"option_{ident}.png", dpi=160, bbox_inches="tight")
+    plt.close(fig)
+
+    first = data.loc[data["year"] == 2013].iloc[0][column]
+    last = data.loc[data["year"] == 2025].iloc[0][column]
+    options.append(
+        {
+            "id": ident,
+            "metric": style["metric"],
+            "denominator": style["denominator"],
+            "grouping": style["grouping"],
+            "chart_type": style["chart_type"],
+            "reason": style["reason"],
+            "probability": style["probability"],
+            "answer": style["answer_template"].format(a=first, b=last),
+            "interpretation": style["interpretation"],
+        }
+    )
+
+(OUT / "options.json").write_text(
+    json.dumps({"options": options}, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n",
+    encoding="utf-8",
+)
+print(data.to_string(index=False))
*** End Patch

Index: /Users/yubo/Documents/Honda/poppy-sandbox/E010/D-v2-kfree-openai-gpt-6-luna/I1-r3/build_analysis.py
===================================================================
--- /Users/yubo/Documents/Honda/poppy-sandbox/E010/D-v2-kfree-openai-gpt-6-luna/I1-r3/build_analysis.py
+++ /Users/yubo/Documents/Honda/poppy-sandbox/E010/D-v2-kfree-openai-gpt-6-luna/I1-r3/build_analysis.py
@@ -0,0 +1,136 @@
+from pathlib import Path
+import json
+
+import duckdb
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import pandas as pd
+
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+OUT = ROOT / "out"
+OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+
+query = """
+SELECT
+    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM crash_date)::INTEGER AS year,
+    COUNT(*)::INTEGER AS reported_crashes,
+    SUM(COALESCE(number_of_motorist_killed, 0))::INTEGER AS motorist_deaths,
+    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE COALESCE(number_of_motorist_killed, 0) > 0)::INTEGER
+        AS crashes_with_motorist_death
+FROM read_parquet(?)
+WHERE crash_date >= DATE '2013-01-01' AND crash_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
+GROUP BY 1
+ORDER BY 1
+"""
+data = duckdb.connect().execute(query, [str(ROOT / "data" / "crashes.parquet")]).fetchdf()
+data["motorist_deaths_per_1000_crashes"] = (
+    data["motorist_deaths"] / data["reported_crashes"] * 1000
+)
+data["pct_crashes_with_motorist_death"] = (
+    data["crashes_with_motorist_death"] / data["reported_crashes"] * 100
+)
+
+styles = [
+    {
+        "id": 1,
+        "metric": "Annual count of motorist deaths in reported crashes",
+        "denominator": "None (annual count)",
+        "grouping": "Calendar year",
+        "chart_type": "Line chart",
+        "column": "motorist_deaths",
+        "y_label": "Motorist deaths",
+        "title": "Motorist deaths in NYC reported crashes by year",
+        "reason": "A count directly shows how many motorist deaths were recorded each year, without implying an exposure denominator.",
+        "probability": 0.2,
+        "answer_template": "This data cannot determine deaths per mile; recorded motorist deaths fell from {a} in 2013 to {b} in 2025.",
+        "interpretation": "This framing answers how the annual number of motorist deaths in reported NYC crashes changed, and the chart shows the count fell between 2013 and 2025. A count is defensible as a direct burden measure, but it leaves both driving exposure and per-mile risk unanswered.",
+    },
+    {
+        "id": 2,
+        "metric": "Motorist deaths per 1,000 reported crashes",
+        "denominator": "All police-reported crashes in the same calendar year",
+        "grouping": "Calendar year",
+        "chart_type": "Line chart",
+        "column": "motorist_deaths_per_1000_crashes",
+        "y_label": "Motorist deaths per 1,000 reported crashes",
+        "title": "Motorist deaths per 1,000 NYC reported crashes",
+        "reason": "Normalizing deaths by reported crashes provides a crash-based severity proxy that accounts for changes in crash volume.",
+        "probability": 0.45,
+        "answer_template": "This data cannot determine deaths per mile; deaths per 1,000 reported crashes rose from {a:.2f} in 2013 to {b:.2f} in 2025.",
+        "interpretation": "This framing answers whether motorist deaths changed relative to the volume of reported crashes, and the chart shows this crash-based rate increased between 2013 and 2025. It is defensible for comparing fatality burden per reported crash, but does not measure travel exposure or deaths per mile driven.",
+    },
+    {
+        "id": 3,
+        "metric": "Share of reported crashes with at least one motorist death",
+        "denominator": "All police-reported crashes in the same calendar year",
+        "grouping": "Calendar year",
+        "chart_type": "Line chart",
+        "column": "pct_crashes_with_motorist_death",
+        "y_label": "Crashes with a motorist death (%)",
+        "title": "Share of NYC reported crashes with a motorist death",
+        "reason": "The fatal-crash share measures how often a reported crash involved a motorist death, without counting multiple deaths in one crash multiple times.",
+        "probability": 0.35,
+        "answer_template": "This data cannot determine deaths per mile; the share of reported crashes with a motorist death rose from {a:.3f}% in 2013 to {b:.3f}% in 2025.",
+        "interpretation": "This framing answers how frequently a police-reported crash involved any motorist death, and the chart shows that share increased between 2013 and 2025. It is defensible as a crash-level fatality measure, but it leaves vehicle-miles traveled and the per-mile risk unanswered.",
+    },
+]
+
+options = []
+for style in styles:
+    ident = style["id"]
+    column = style["column"]
+    values = data[["year", column]].copy()
+    values.columns = ["year", style["metric"].replace(" ", "_").lower()]
+    # Keep the metric and its denominator visible in the plotted data for auditability.
+    if ident == 1:
+        values["reported_crashes"] = data["reported_crashes"]
+    elif ident == 2:
+        values["motorist_deaths"] = data["motorist_deaths"]
+        values["reported_crashes"] = data["reported_crashes"]
+    else:
+        values["crashes_with_motorist_death"] = data["crashes_with_motorist_death"]
+        values["reported_crashes"] = data["reported_crashes"]
+    csv_path = OUT / f"values_{ident}.csv"
+    values.to_csv(csv_path, index=False, float_format="%.6f")
+
+    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5.3))
+    ax.plot(data["year"], data[column], marker="o", linewidth=2, color="#1769aa")
+    ax.set_xticks(data["year"])
+    ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=45)
+    ax.set_ylabel(style["y_label"])
+    ax.set_xlabel("Crash year")
+    ax.set_title(style["title"])
+    ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.3)
+    ax.text(
+        0.01,
+        -0.24,
+        "Source: NYC police-reported crash records. This dataset does not include miles driven.",
+        transform=ax.transAxes,
+        fontsize=8,
+        color="#555555",
+    )
+    fig.tight_layout()
+    fig.savefig(OUT / f"option_{ident}.png", dpi=160, bbox_inches="tight")
+    plt.close(fig)
+
+    first = data.loc[data["year"] == 2013].iloc[0][column]
+    last = data.loc[data["year"] == 2025].iloc[0][column]
+    options.append(
+        {
+            "id": ident,
+            "metric": style["metric"],
+            "denominator": style["denominator"],
+            "grouping": style["grouping"],
+            "chart_type": style["chart_type"],
+            "reason": style["reason"],
+            "probability": style["probability"],
+            "answer": style["answer_template"].format(a=first, b=last),
+            "interpretation": style["interpretation"],
+        }
+    )
+
+(OUT / "options.json").write_text(
+    json.dumps({"options": options}, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n",
+    encoding="utf-8",
+)
+print(data.to_string(index=False))
